summary: Malawi admits citizens of about 40 countries — mostly its SADC and Commonwealth neighbours — visa-free. Since February 2026 the US, UK, EU and most other passports can get a visa on arrival, while a list of Category One countries must obtain a visa before departure through the official eVisa portal.

notes: Change money only at banks and licensed forex bureaus — street exchange is illegal, and kwacha are effectively impossible to exchange outside Malawi.

payments.text: Cash dominates. Cards work at upmarket lodges, city hotels and larger supermarkets, but almost nowhere else. Carry US dollars to change at banks or forex bureaus, and small kwacha notes for daily spending.

safety.text: Malawi lives up to its "warm heart of Africa" reputation and violent crime against tourists is rare. Petty theft, bag snatching and scams occur in cities and on beaches. The usual precautions apply, and avoid driving after dark.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The May–October dry season is best: cooler and green May to August, hot and excellent for wildlife September–October. The rains run roughly November to April, when some park roads become impassable.

idp.text: Malawi is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

driving.text: Malawi is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Malawi yet.

tips.text: Lake Malawi carries a bilharzia (schistosomiasis) risk in some shoreline areas. Swimming is part of the experience for many visitors. Ask locally about safer stretches and consider a post-trip test if you swam.
Malaria is present year-round throughout Malawi, including the lakeshore. Take prophylaxis, use repellent and sleep under nets.

Bring US dollars in good condition and change them at banks or licensed bureaus. Keep the receipts. Kwacha are effectively worthless outside Malawi, so change back what you don't need before departure.
Power cuts are common and fuel shortages happen periodically — lodges run generators, but keep devices charged and don't let your tank run low on long drives.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Malawi?
faq.answer: Most visitors do. About 40 nationalities — including South Africa, Zambia, Kenya, Ghana and Singapore — enter visa-free. Citizens of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, the EU and most other countries can buy a visa on arrival (USD 75 single entry on the Department of Immigration fee table) or apply in advance at evisa.gov.mw, while Category One countries such as India, China and Nigeria must get a visa before departure.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Malawi and can I extend?
faq.answer: Single-entry visas are normally granted for 30 days. You can extend at regional immigration offices in Lilongwe, Blantyre or Mzuzu, typically up to a total of 90 days for tourism.

faq.question: Can I still get a Malawi visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, for nationals of the Category Two countries, which include the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the EU: a public notice effective 24 February 2026 makes them eligible at all designated ports of entry, and tells airlines to board them without a visa. Bring US dollars in cash. Category One nationals must still obtain a visa before departure, and the government encourages everyone to apply in advance at evisa.gov.mw.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Malawi?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from — or transit more than 12 hours in — a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Arriving directly from Europe, North America or southern Africa, no certificate is required.

faq.question: Is it safe to swim in Lake Malawi?
faq.answer: Millions do, but parts of the lake carry bilharzia (schistosomiasis), and crocodiles and hippos frequent some shores. Stick to beaches recommended by your lodge, and consider a bilharzia test 6–8 weeks after your trip if you swam.
